assets.purpose: animations (shared by all players, enemies and bosses)
assets.contents_summary: Parsed the GLB JSON chunks. Each file has 1 skin with 23 bones, and every file includes a T-Pose clip in its count. Medium counts: MovementBasic 11 (Jump_*, Running_A/B, Walking_A/B/C), MovementAdvanced 13 (Dodge x4, Running_Strafe_L/R, Running_HoldingBow/Rifle, Crouching, Sneaking, Walking_Backwards), General 15 (Idle_A/B, Hit_A/B, Death_A/B, Spawn_Air/Ground, Throw, Use_Item), CombatMelee 22 (Melee_1H/2H/Dualwield/Unarmed/Block*), CombatRanged 20 (Ranged_1H/2H Aim/Shoot/Reload, Ranged_Bow_*, Ranged_Magic_Raise/Shoot/Spellcasting/Spellcasting_Long/Summon), Special 15 (Skeletons_Awaken/Resurrect/Taunt). Also Simulation 14 and Tools 29, which are not needed. Large counts: CombatMelee 16 (Melee_1H_Slash, Melee_2H_Slam, Melee_Unarmed_Smash, Melee_Dualwield_SlashCombo, Block, Kick, Punch...), General 6 (Idle_A/B, Hit_A, Death_A), MovementBasic 3 (only Running_A and Walking_A), MovementAdvanced 5 (4 dodges, which the research missed).
assets.notes: Bone check: I compared bone name sets and rest translation and rotation against Rig_Medium_MovementBasic. All 23 bone names and rest poses match exactly (0.0000 difference) for every Medium character in 2.0 and Series 4-6, every Skeleton 1.1 and every 1.0 Adventurer and Skeleton. Joint order differs between files, which does not matter because Godot binds tracks by bone name. CORRECTION 1: Rig_Large has no jump, strafe, spellcast or ranged clips, so bosses are melee-only unless you borrow Medium clips. CORRECTION 2: every clip keys translation on every bone. In all Large characters (BlackKnight, FrostGolem, OrcBrute, Monstrosity, Clanker, Skeleton_Golem, Barbarian_Large, 4GTN) the head bone rests at y=1.1405, but Rig_Large clips key the head at y=1.0255, so the head sinks about 0.115 m into the body. Fix it in Godot import: on the Rig_Large animations, enable Retarget > Remove Tracks > Unimportant Positions (keep only root and hips position), or strip the non-hips position tracks with a script. Only Mannequin_Large matches the library exactly.

LARGE (hips y=1.041): adventurers-2.0/Characters/gltf/Barbarian_Large.glb, series-5 BlackKnight, FrostGolem and Clanker, series-6 OrcBrute and Monstrosity, skeletons-1.1 Skeleton_Golem, plus 4GTN and 4GTN_Forgotten (21 bones, no handslot bones).
assets.notes: Corrections. (a) The research named 'Rig_Medium' for every character, but BlackKnight, FrostGolem, OrcBrute, Monstrosity, Clanker and Skeleton_Golem are Large-rig only. There is no Medium BlackKnight. (b) Werewolf_Wolf is on the Medium biped rig. (c) 4GTN has no handslot bones, so it can't hold weapons through BoneAttachment3D on handslot.r; attach to hand.r instead. (d) Caveman exists and is valid for Grappler; the research left it out of its contents list. (e) The paths contain spaces and long names, so copy the selected files into short res:// folders in the Godot project. The 2.0 and 1.0 Adventurer characters also share an identical core rig: the 1.0 files add 18 IK/control bones (kneeIK, handIK and so on), which the 2.0 clips simply don't key, so 2.0 libraries also drive the 1.0 characters.

recommendation:
VERDICT: The research holds up. Licenses, file presence and rigging are confirmed, with 4 corrections.

WHAT I VERIFIED
- Licenses: I read all 3 mirror licenses (KayKit-CC0-License.txt, "The Complete KayKit Collection v6", CC0, commercial use OK), the 3 official KayKit LICENSE.txt files and the Kenney license.txt files. All are CC0.
- Rigging: I parsed the GLB JSON of 110 GLB files, reading only the files and executing nothing from the downloads. Every character has 1 skin. The 2.0 and mirror characters have 0 embedded animations. The 1.0 Adventurers have 76 each and the 1.0 Skeletons 95 each.
- glTF references: I checked every buffer and texture URI in 62 weapon .gltf files and 283 dungeon .gltf files. None are missing.

SKELETON COMPATIBILITY
- Medium rig: every Medium character has exactly the same 23 bone names and rest transforms as Rig_Medium_*.glb (0.0000 difference). That includes Adventurers 2.0, Series 4-6, Skeletons 1.1, Adventurers 1.0 and Skeletons 1.0.
- Joint order: it differs between files, but Godot binds tracks by bone name, so that is harmless.
- Result: one shared AnimationLibrary set works for all players and trash mobs.

CORRECTIONS
1. The 1.0 rig has 41 bones: the 23 core bones plus 18 IK/control bones. It is compatible with the 2.0 clips but not literally the same hierarchy.
2. Large-rig bosses have a head offset problem. These are BlackKnight, FrostGolem, OrcBrute, Monstrosity, Clanker, Skeleton_Golem, Barbarian_Large and 4GTN.
   - Their head bone rests at y=1.1405.
   - Rig_Large clips key the head translation at a constant 1.0255.
   - Played as-is, the head sinks about 0.115 m into the body.
   - Fix in Godot import: Retarget > Remove Tracks > Unimportant Positions, or strip position tracks except root and hips.
   - Only Mannequin_Large matches the library exactly.
3. Rig_Large has only these clips:
   - CombatMelee: 16
   - General: 6
   - MovementBasic: 3 (Running_A and Walking_A only)
   - MovementAdvanced: 5 dodges
   - It has no jump, cast or ranged clips. Boss skills need VFX-driven attacks or custom clips.
4. 4GTN has no handslot bones. Attach its weapons to hand.r.

Also note: BlackKnight, FrostGolem, OrcBrute and Monstrosity exist only on the Large rig. Caveman, which the research left out of its contents list, does exist on the Medium rig.

- Import one Rig_Medium character, then save each Rig_Medium_*.glb's animations as AnimationLibrary .res files and add them to one AnimationPlayer per character.
- Weapons attach with BoneAttachment3D on handslot.r and handslot.l.
- The 2.0 clip names are Melee_1H_Attack_Chop, Ranged_Magic_Shoot and so on. Every file contains a T-Pose clip; ignore it.
